purpose: Preserve the ingest-side domain invariants of the Portal's single SQLite Operational Store through deep transactional operations: Sender Installation lifecycle records, one-use enrollment codes, capability generations, exact archival of accepted Outbox Messages, Delivery Block and sequence-gap evidence, Sync Checkpoint history, the storage reserve, coherent current-state reads, and each delivery cycle's state derived from archived rows, so callers validate fragment continuity and completions without replaying archived envelopes.

inputs.name: domain_transactions
inputs.description: Caller-supplied lifecycle intents, enrollment-code digests, capability advertisements, accepted-message archival records with exact envelope and receipt bytes, and Delivery Block records, each carrying a timezone-aware Portal time.

inputs.name: database_file
inputs.description: The one SQLite database file at a deployment-chosen path, with its write-ahead log, either absent or created by this or a later store version.

inputs.name: free_space
inputs.description: Free bytes on the database file's filesystem compared with the deployment-configured storage reserve at the moment of each archival transaction.

inputs.name: sqlite_runtime
inputs.description: The SQLite library version linked into the running Python interpreter.

outputs.name: opened_store
outputs.description: A store handle on a database at exactly the baseline schema, with WAL journaling, synchronous FULL, and foreign keys enforced, or a named startup refusal.

outputs.name: archive_result
outputs.description: The Delivery Receipt bytes committed with a newly archived message, or the identical prior receipt for an identical retry with no write.

outputs.name: lifecycle_record
outputs.description: An append-only Sender Installation lifecycle event and the resulting installation state.

outputs.name: coherent_view
outputs.description: Reads served from one SQLite read transaction: installation states and operational facts, accepted envelopes in sequence order, archived items, honored capability generations, sequence gaps, Delivery Blocks, paginated Sync Checkpoint history, storage-reserve status, and one delivery cycle's last archived fragment, chain inputs, counts, and completion.

outputs.name: store_refusal
outputs.description: A named refusal that leaves the database exactly as it was before the operation.

observable_effects.name: operational-database-writes
observable_effects.description: Committed SQLite transactions on the Operational Store file and its write-ahead log; a refused or failed operation commits nothing.

owns: the baseline SQLite schema, its recorded checksummed migration, and connection durability settings
transactional invariants for one active or draining Sender Installation, one-use enrollment codes, and append-only lifecycle events
exact envelope and per-item archival, sequence uniqueness and ordering, sequence-gap evidence, and Last Delivery
capability generation monotonicity and the rule that a generation stops being honored only after a later generation's acknowledgement is archived
health-data-free Delivery Block and Sync Checkpoint history records
storage-reserve enforcement at write time and coherent read snapshots
deriving each delivery cycle's last archived fragment, its chain inputs, its fragment and record counts, and its completion from archived rows, without a schema change
does_not_own: wire decoding, delivery evaluation, chain calculation, receipts, or compatibility decisions
Operator intent, enrollment-offer issuance, or when lifecycle transitions happen
Polling Freshness classification or clock-skew conditions
Source Record identity, reconciliation, processing, summaries, policies, cutovers, deletion, export, or backup
upgrading an existing database to a later schema
HTTP ingress, Authorized Ingress, or the deployment's reserve value
